name: After recital 1
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the Union Civil Protection Mechanism and Union support for health emergency preparedness and response, and repealing Decision No 1313/2013/EU (Union Civil Protection Mechanism)
part_text: (6a) Particular attention should be paid to least favoured territories, i.e. territories with geographical specificities, that suffer from natural or demographic handicaps, and that face economic, social and structural constraints including, rural areas, mountain regions, northernmost, isolated and sparsely populated areas, islands, remote, border and cross-border regions, as well as outermost regions. These territories might face specific vulnerabilities in cross-border crises, including limitations in transport connectivity, emergency medical access, energy resilience, communications interoperability and surge capacity, significantly hampering response to disasters. Member States and regions located at the external borders of the Union may also face a disproportionate burden in situations of large-scale crises, including sudden inflows of displaced persons, hybrid threats or cross-border health emergencies. In this context, prevention, preparedness and response measures under the Union Mechanism should take those territorial specificities into account, in particular with a view to improving cross-border coordination, interoperability, joint planning, operational coordination and timely assistance to affected populations. Joint planning, exercises and data sharing between neighbouring regions shall be supported financially.
